The big-box run: volume converts to 2-cubic-foot bags so the car is loaded once, correctly, instead of twice in the rain.
Contractors price mulch by volume installed. Area-and-depth arithmetic is the quote's spine — defensible to clients because it is just geometry.
Two inches refreshes colour; three to four suppresses weeds. The volume difference between the two choices, priced before the order, is this page's most-used comparison.
500 sq ft × 2 in: 500 × (2/12) = 83.3 ft³ = 3.09 yd³ ≈ 42 bags of 2 ft³. Add a settling margin and the order becomes 3.5 yards bulk — the margin is cheaper than a second delivery.
A cubic yard (27 ft³) covers 108 sq ft at 3 inches, 162 at 2 inches, 324 at 1 inch. Memorise the 108 and most garden-centre math becomes mental arithmetic.

popular_table.note: Volumes are loose (fluffed) as sold. Mulch compacts and decomposes — depths settle roughly 20–30% in the first season, which the margin FAQ addresses.

faq: How much extra should I order for settling?
Ten to twenty percent over the computed volume is the trade habit for bark and wood mulches; dyed and rubber mulches settle less. Over-ordering slightly beats the second-trip surcharge every time.
Bulk or bags — which is cheaper?

Bulk wins beyond roughly 2–3 cubic yards in most markets (a yard is 13–14 standard bags); bags win on convenience, cleanliness and small jobs. The calculator reports both quantities so the price comparison is yours to make.

Three inches is the working standard for weed suppression and moisture; 2 inches for a colour refresh over existing mulch; 4 inches for new beds on bare soil. Deeper than 4 risks sour, anaerobic mulch — more is not better past the point.
Play areas use engineered wood fibre at greater depths for fall safety (standards specify by fall height) — that is a safety specification, not a gardening depth, and it has its own product class.
Can I enter the bed as length × width?
Yes — rectangular beds directly; irregular beds by their measured area from the Map Area Calculator. The depth math does not care how the area arrived.
Stone and gravel instead of mulch?
The volume arithmetic is identical — only the product changes (and the weight: a yard of stone runs well over a ton). The Soil Volume Calculator is the sibling for soil and fill.
Measure what's there and subtract: refreshing 1 inch of surviving mulch to a 3-inch standard needs 2 inches of new — enter the difference as the depth.
